name: Aarhus University
about: Aarhus University has roughly 38,000 students and a park campus of yellow-brick buildings that runs right into the middle of town. Almost everything it teaches at bachelor level is in Danish; five programmes are taught in English, all in Aarhus itself and one, Economics and Business Administration, also in the small town of Herning an hour west; all of them are in computing, economics or cognitive science. AU is also unusually explicit about the numbers: every programme page publishes last year's quota 1 cut-off, the standby cut-off and the admission area number.

languageOfInstruction.note: A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

ibEquivalences.subject: Social Studies
ibEquivalences.note: AU's own addition to the Agency's table: "Global Politics HL: Recognised as Social Science B"; "Global Politics SL: Recognised as Social Science B in combination with Economics SL/HL". Page revised 21.08.2026, read 25 Sep 2026.

levelRaise.text: AU accepts supplementary courses passed before 5 July, and up to two passed after it as conditional admission (documentation by 5 September). It also counts College Board AP and British A-level courses as A level.
levelRaise.multiple: AU accepts as many as you need passed before 5 July, and at most two passed after it.

admissionRoutes.short: an assessment of your subject grades and experience
admissionRoutes.text: AU assesses the average of your grades in the programme's quota 2 subjects, and can add to it for documented relevant experience (work, internships, a folk high school; 4–12 months). Everything must be documented by 15 March.

notes: A, B and C are Danish subject levels, not grades. AU repeats this on each programme page: "B-level is the Danish subject level, not the grade."

AU attaches a converted-GPA floor to quota 1 on five of the six English-taught programmes: you need at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale in your qualifying examination to be assessed in quota 1 at all. Below that, your application can only go through quota 2. Economics and Business Administration in Herning does not state such a floor.
Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development add a second floor: a minimum GPA of 6.0 in Mathematics A specifically, on top of the overall 6.0.
The 6.0 floor is not the cut-off. The cut-off is what the last admitted applicant actually scored, and in 2026 that was 11.4 for Computer Science and 11.2 for Data Science.

AU tells "Danish applicants" (on its Data Science page, "applicants with Danish A") to treat the English-taught Computer Science, Data Science and IT Product Development degrees as the harder route and to apply to the Danish-taught equivalents (Datalogi, Datavidenskab, It-produktudvikling) as well. For Data Science AU says outright that the English version "is intended for international students". The two versions lead to the same English-taught master's.

The standby cut-off is published next to the quota 1 cut-off and is usually lower — dramatically so for IT Product Development in 2026 (10.1 in quota 1, 6.9 for standby). You have to tick standby when you apply, and the standby application deadline is 5 July.

Herning is not Aarhus. AU Herning is a small campus roughly an hour west of Aarhus in a town of about 50,000, running a few business, engineering and technology programmes. Its Economics and Business Administration degree is academically similar to the Aarhus one but had a 2026 cut-off of 6.9 against 9.2.

Non-EU/EEA students should read the paying-applicant rule before anything else: the 15 March documentation deadline means you cannot be assessed on results you receive in July, so a May 2027 IB candidate who is a paying applicant would need to apply a year later.
